items.bold: IRAN SUBMITTED 14-POINT PROPOSAL: end war in 30 days, new Hormuz mechanism, reparations, US forces withdraw.
items.text: NPR (15hr ago), CNN live (21min ago), and Tasnim confirmed: Iran submitted a 14-point response to the US 15-point framework. Key demands: (1) Resolve all issues and end war within 30 days; (2) Guarantees against future military aggression; (3) Withdrawal of US forces from Iran's periphery; (4) End to naval blockade; (5) Release of frozen Iranian assets; (6) Payment of reparations; (7) Lifting of sanctions; (8) End to fighting in Lebanon; (9) New mechanism governing the Strait of Hormuz. Georgetown University Qatar professor Kamrava (CNN): "What is most important for Iranians, given the state of Iran's economy, are the release of Iranian assets and lifting of sanctions — much more important than coordinating role in the Strait." Iran expert (CNN): the 14-point proposal "contains some non-starter demands that Trump is unlikely to accept — mirroring the maximalist approach Washington has taken throughout."

items.bold: TRUMP TRUTH SOCIAL: "Can't imagine it would be acceptable — Iran has NOT YET PAID A BIG ENOUGH PRICE."
items.text: Euronews (8hr ago) and Business Standard (14hr ago) confirmed: Trump posted on Truth Social after being briefed on Iran's 14-point proposal: "I will soon be reviewing the plan that Iran has just sent to us, but can't imagine that it would be acceptable in that they have not yet paid a big enough price for what they have done to Humanity, and the World, over the last 47 years." This is a significant step back from Saturday morning's "concept of deal, waiting for exact wording" — Trump has added new conditions: Iran must pay a bigger price before any deal. The gap between Saturday morning (positive) and Saturday evening (skeptical) shows Trump's negotiating approach: raise hopes, then add conditions. The proposal is not dead, but Trump's language signals he will not accept Iran's 14-point proposal as-is.

items.bold: TRUMP: "We're sort of like PIRATES" on cargo seizures. Tehran: "damning admission of piracy."
items.text: Al Jazeera (3hr ago) confirmed: At a Florida event Saturday, Trump said: "We took over the cargo. Took over the oil, a very profitable business. Who would have thought, we're sort of like pirates, but we're not playing games." Tehran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs immediately seized on the remarks, labelling them a "damning admission of piracy." Under international maritime law, seizing neutral ships and their cargo without a legal basis constitutes piracy. Trump's "pirates" comment — likely rhetorical — hands Iran a significant propaganda victory and complicates the US's legal position on the blockade. Iran has already argued the US blockade violates UNCLOS (UN Convention on the Law of the Sea).

military.t: IRAN SUBMITTED 14-POINT PROPOSAL — New Hormuz Mechanism, Reparations, US Forces Withdraw.
military.d: NPR (15hr ago), CNN (21min ago), and Tasnim/Fars confirmed: Iran submitted a 14-point response to the US 15-point framework via Pakistan. Key points: (1) Resolve all issues and end war within 30 days; (2) Guarantees against future US/Israeli aggression; (3) Withdrawal of US forces from Iran's periphery; (4) End to naval blockade; (5) Release of frozen Iranian assets; (6) Payment of reparations; (7) Lifting of sanctions; (8) End to fighting in Lebanon; (9) New mechanism governing the Strait of Hormuz. Georgetown Professor Kamrava (CNN): asset release and sanctions lifting most important for Iran — "Hormuz is more of a bargaining chip." Iran expert (CNN): the proposal contains "non-starter demands mirroring the maximalist approach Washington has taken." The 14-point vs 15-point framing signals both sides are in opening-position mode — the real negotiation has not yet started.

military.t: TRUMP: "Can't Imagine Acceptable — Iran Has NOT YET PAID A BIG ENOUGH PRICE." Skeptical Truth Social.

This walks back his morning "concept of deal, waiting for exact wording" optimism. Trump is now conditioning any deal on Iran paying a bigger price — adding a new condition on top of the nuclear demand. The proposal is not dead — Trump said he will "soon be reviewing" it — but his language signals it will not be accepted as-is. This is also Trump's maximalist opening position in the negotiation: anchor high, then negotiate down.

military.t: TRUMP: "We're Sort of Like Pirates." Tehran: "Damning Admission of Piracy." Iran Parliament Formalising Hormuz Law.

assessment.body:
Sunday 8:15 PM IST. Day 65. The proposals are on the table. The gap is wide. Both sides are posturing.

IRAN'S 14-POINT PROPOSAL — WHAT IT SAYS
• End war within 30 days (vs US 2-month ceasefire proposal)
• Guarantees: Israel + US cannot attack again
• US forces withdraw from Iran's periphery
• Naval blockade ends
• Iran's frozen assets released
• Reparations paid
• Sanctions lifted
• End to fighting in Lebanon
• New mechanism governing the Strait of Hormuz
Response to US 15-point framework — both sides opening with maximum positions

TRUMP'S TRUTH SOCIAL — THE PIVOT BACK
• Morning (Air Force One): "concept of deal, waiting for exact wording" — positive
• Evening (Truth Social): "can't imagine it would be acceptable"
• "Iran has not yet paid a big enough price for what they have done to Humanity over the last 47 years"
• This is not a rejection — Trump said he "will soon be reviewing" the plan
• This is Trump anchoring high: Iran must pay more before any deal

THE PIRACY MOMENT
• Trump at Florida: "We're sort of like pirates, but we're not playing games"
• Tehran MFA: "damning admission of piracy" — hands Iran a legal and propaganda win
• Complicates US legal position on blockade under UNCLOS

THE GAS PRICE PRESSURE — THE REAL NEGOTIATING DRIVER
• US gasoline: $4.45/gallon (AAA Saturday)
• Up $1.47 since war began February 28
• Up 34 cents in ONE WEEK
• November 2026 midterms approaching
• Washington Post: "Trump running out of options"
• This domestic pressure is the single biggest force pushing Trump toward a deal

IRAN PARLIAMENT FORMALISING HORMUZ LAW
• Iran parliament set to approve law restricting Hormuz vessel passage
• Formalises toll system and vessel screening into domestic statute
• Permanent Iranian Hormuz control becoming law — regardless of any deal

INDIA'S MONDAY MORNING
• Markets reopen 9:15 AM IST
• Trump skepticism limits deal rally
• Brent $108-111 — elevated but off peak
• State elections May 4 = additional catalyst
• OMC hike likely this week
• Iran Hormuz law = permanent toll system for India tankers

VERDICT: Day 65 evening shows the West Asia War entering its proposal-and-counter-proposal phase in earnest. Iran's 14-point proposal is maximalist — reparations, US force withdrawal, new Hormuz mechanism. Trump's response is also maximalist — "not paid big enough price." Both sides are anchoring far apart. But the real negotiation — driven by $4.45 gas at home for Trump and a devastated economy for Iran — is beginning in the space between these maximalist positions. India's Monday markets will trade the gap: cautious recovery if talks continue, sharp selloff if either side walks away.
